items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: Alexander Smallens conducted the show... I stepped over the footlights and said, 'Mr. Smallens, if I had the money for the way you conduct, I'd be a millionaire,' which made him feel more in keeping with going along with me.

ctx.x: Could you start over one more time?

It was in 1935 when I was chosen by the immortal George Gershwin to do the character of Sportin' Life in his new folk opera "Porgy and Bess," at the Alvin Theater in New York City in 1935 and we were to rehearse in different places, the show before and the show going on, naturally, as you might know and we did and it was on the dress rehearsal night when Alexander Smallens had decided that I wouldn't fit the show, because he had given me a down beat and I didn't take it, I was right behind his beat and he threw…

baton to start to conduct and just as he stepped before the orchestra to conduct, I stepped over the footlights and said, "Mr. Smallens, if I had the money for the way you conduct, I'd be a millionaire," which made him feel more in keeping with going along with me. But Gershwin knew I could do the numbers, I could do the entire show. That's why he picked me.
